questions.q: What two things must __init__ declare for a custom gym.Env subclass to be usable by generic RL code?
options: A render mode and a random seed
observation_space and action_space
A reward function and a discount factor
A neural network and an optimizer
questions.explain: Declaring observation_space and action_space is what lets algorithm code, like a policy network's input layer or an action sampler, work with any compliant environment.

questions.q: Why does reset(seed=None, options=None) call super().reset(seed=seed)?
options: It is purely optional boilerplate with no effect
It reseeds the environment's own random number generator so that passing the same seed twice produces reproducible starting states
It automatically registers the environment
It sets the action_space to Discrete
questions.explain: Calling the base class's reset with the seed ensures the environment's internal RNG is reseeded, which is what makes reproducible episodes possible.

questions.q: A custom environment adds its own max-steps counter and ends the episode when the counter is hit. How should that ending be reported?
options: terminated=True, truncated=False
terminated=False, truncated=True
Both set to True regardless of cause
Neither — just stop calling step()
questions.explain: A step cap is an external limit, not the environment's own dynamics ending the episode, so it should be reported as truncated, not terminated.

questions.q: What does Gymnasium's check_env() function do?
options: Trains a baseline agent on the environment to benchmark difficulty
Automatically renders the environment for visual inspection
Runs automated checks for common contract violations, like mismatched space shapes, wrong dtypes, or non-reproducible seeding
Converts a single environment into a vectorized one
questions.explain: check_env() is a built-in checker that catches the most common ways a custom environment violates the Gymnasium API contract before you waste time debugging a learning algorithm instead.

questions.q: After writing and checking a custom environment class, what does register() let you do?
options: Skip writing a step() method entirely
Create the environment by string ID through gym.make(), just like a built-in environment
Automatically vectorize the environment
Bypass the observation_space declaration
questions.explain: register() associates an ID with the environment's entry point, so gym.make("MyEnv-v0") can construct it exactly as it would a built-in Gymnasium environment.
